scope: Windows release engineering, signing and isolated NSIS candidate QA
changes: Unsigned files, appId, NSIS GUID, executable, package/updater cache, default install root and userData identities are separate; no shortcuts/associations. Output release/unsigned-test-build preserves original release/win-unpacked and actual user shortcut; signed candidate uses release/signed-release.
Flavor resource records x64/version/identity/commit and formal approval hash. afterPack builds exact regular-file removal whitelist and rejects linked inputs.

NSIS only removes known packaged files; RMDir is nonrecursive and preserves unknown contents. Both explicit appData-deletion flags and unsafe legacy registered uninstallers are blocked. Init, VerifyInstDir and a hidden final preflight Section run before old-uninstaller execution or extraction.

Installer smoke requires verified unsigned flavor/current installer SHA and no preexisting test registry. It first rejects unrelated nonempty fixture target; then install/repair/app smoke/data-delete rejection/uninstall preserve actual SQLite quick_check/hash and valid synthetic video inside/outside installation and temporary profile. It checks production registration/shortcut hash unchanged.

Metadata verifies real Authenticode for installer/application/NativeHost and expected publisher/timestamp for formal candidates, reads explicit system Security module, writes exact current candidate SHA256SUMS and metadata. It does not need certificate payloads.

Formal build is fail-closed on repository approval manifest false, pending LICENSE, ownership/license/lock/native binary/source evidence hashes and clean Windows11/previous signed upgrade QA evidence. Default template grants no license and is unapproved.

Release Actions use root-verified immutable SHAs and no persisted Git credentials; unsigned test QA has no signing secrets. Formal protected job exposes certificate/password only to signing build steps, not npm ci/postinstall or metadata/upload. Owned NativeHost/app/installer signing is required; third-party FFmpeg/FFprobe binary bytes preserved.

Artifact gate verifies actual nonempty x64 PE files, exact SQLite/FFmpeg/FFprobe/NativeHost inputs, Electron/Chromium and FFmpeg notices; no mere directory-existence claims. Missing user-supplied libmpv remains an explicit capability limit.

remainingRisks: Full GPL FFmpeg/FFprobe exact corresponding-source/dependency provenance remains unapproved; current executable pair includes FFprobe4.0.2. Root licensing report retains formal release blocker.
A safe new uninstaller cannot fix a previously installed recursive uninstaller. Such upgrades are blocked, not declared supported; actual previous signed version/clean Win11 testing remains required.

File-lock preflight is not an atomic upgrade rollback or proof against same-user malicious races/power loss. NSIS known-file removal may partially complete if a later file becomes locked; unknown user files are retained.

NativeHost existing C# compiler output may include build time; binary approval must target concrete candidate or future reproducible-build/signing-input reuse. Recompilation is not silently covered by a previous hash approval.
Protected GitHub public-release environment/reviewers and approval variables must actually be configured by owner; workflow text is not evidence that remote protection exists.
Only template/static/unit verification has been completed for installer guards so far. Do not claim unknown install-file preservation or installer PASS until actual isolated NSIS test completes.
